quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #13
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 22

questions.question: Excessive speed:

options.text: Does not increase the chance of a crash.
Increases your ability to react to a hazard.
Often leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often leads to dangerous driving decisions.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a common cause of vehicle crashes. It does not save time and often leads to dangerous driving decisions.

questions.question: You should always travel:

options.text: At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.
At the speed limit.
At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Your speed should match the road conditions, weather, and the legal speed limit. Never drive above the speed limit. Slow down when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Yellow lines separate:

options.text: Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines mark the center of a two-way road. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass if it is safe.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad ahead.
No passing zone.
School zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Your vehicle's wheels have run off the edge of the pavement. What should you do first?

options.text: Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge the car back onto the pavement.
Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes. Slow down, check traffic, and safely return to the road. Do not jerk the wheel sharply, as this can cause you to lose control or enter other lanes.

questions.question: Allow extra space in front of your vehicle when following a:

options.text: Station wagon.
Passenger vehicle.
Motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles can stop faster than cars, and you need room to stop if the rider brakes suddenly or falls. Motorcycles are also hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Which statement is true about driving and taking medications?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
Medications are safe to take at any time, if prescribed by a doctor.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: All medications—prescription or over-the-counter—can affect your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can make you drowsy. You must know how your medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not drive through the flooded area. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive through a flooded road. Water may hide hazards even if it looks shallow. Turn around and find another route to your destination.

questions.question: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.
Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.
Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop. Position yourself parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: What message will be found on this yellow pennant-shaped sign?

options.text: Right turns only.
Right turns permitted.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: No passing zone.
questions.explanation: Yellow pennant-shaped signs mark a no passing zone.

questions.question: When bad weather makes it hard to see, you should:

options.text: Speed up to leave the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Stay farther behind the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther behind the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: When you cannot see clearly due to darkness or bad weather, increase the distance between your car and the one ahead. This gives you more time to react to dangers you may not see.

questions.question: When a bicyclist turns left:

options.text: They may use the left lane.
They may cut through all lanes.
They may wait on the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may use the left lane.
questions.explanation: Bicyclists ride with traffic on the road. You should expect to see a bicyclist using the left lane when turning.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should:

options.text: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
Slow down and use your high beam headlights.
Turn your lights on and off to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, slow down and use your low beam headlights. If you cannot see ahead, pull off the road and wait for the fog to clear.

questions.question: You must show proof of insurance to law enforcement:

options.text: Only if you were in a crash.
If you were in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
Only if you are stopped and given a ticket.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you were in a crash or stopped for a ticket.
questions.explanation: You must carry proof of insurance whenever you drive. Show your proof of insurance and license to an officer whenever they ask after a traffic stop or crash.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you:

options.text: May turn after slowing down and checking for traffic.
Cannot turn until the light turns green.
May turn after coming to a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: Stopping distance and crash severity:

options.text: Decrease as you drive faster.
Are not affected by how fast you drive.
Increase as you drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase as you drive faster.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the more severe a crash will be.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from the side with the solid yellow line.
Not allowed from either side.
Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allowed from the side with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: When one side has a solid yellow line and the other has a broken yellow line, you may pass from the side with the broken line only.

questions.question: When exiting the freeway on a curving downhill ramp, you should:

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Start braking once you enter the curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You cannot see hazards ahead clearly, and braking while turning may cause your car to skid.

questions.question: At an intersection with stop signs on all four corners, yield to any driver:

options.text: On your left.
Who got there first.
Across from you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Who got there first.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles should go through in the order they arrived. If two cars arrive at the same time, the car on the right goes first.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Look out the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look out the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, put your right arm on the passenger seat and look directly out the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors because they cannot show what is directly behind your car. Always back up slowly.

questions.question: Which statement is correct?

options.text: Use your left foot to brake.
Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
You should brake hard to stop quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
questions.explanation: Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating. Press the brakes gently and gradually so your vehicle stops smoothly.

questions.question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?

options.text: Motorcycles do not follow the same rules as other vehicles.
A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
Motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle can stop much faster than a car.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can stop quickly. Following too closely puts you and the rider in danger. You need time and space to avoid a crash if the motorcycle suddenly stops.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your speed the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Signs in construction zones warn you about workers, slow equipment, and closed lanes. Reduce your speed and be prepared to slow down or stop.

questions.question: At an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:

options.text: Wait for the green light before going.
Slow down and cross carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be careful. Watch for other cars and pedestrians crossing.

questions.question: A double solid yellow line down the center of a road means passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.
